summary: Boris Ivanovich Klyuev was an indologist and linguist who studied at Moscow State University. He worked at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (1952–1971), the CPSU Central Committee (1971–1982), MGIMO (1982–1988), and the Institute of Oriental Studies (1988).

Boris Ivanovich Pankratov was a scholar of Sinology, Tibetology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies who studied at the Eastern Institute. His career included posts at Far Eastern Federal University, the Harvard-Yenching Institute, the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts, and Saint Petersburg State University.

Boris Karpushkin was an indologist and linguist who studied at the Moscow Institute of Oriental Studies. He served as a naučnyj sotrudnik at the Institute of Oriental Studies (1961–1974) and taught at MGIMO beginning in 1974.

Boris Leonidovič Smirnov was an Indologist who studied at the S. M. Kirov Military Medical Academy. He served as director of Turkmen State Medical University (1939–1956) and was a member of the Academy of Sciences of Turkmenistan (1951–1967).

Boris Mikhailovich Lyapunov was a linguist who studied at Saint Petersburg State University under Vatroslav Jagić and Filipp Fedorovich Fortunatov. He held posts at the University of Kharkiv, Odesa University (1899–1923), and Saint Petersburg State University (1924).

Boris Stavisky was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Saint Petersburg State University and Saint Petersburg State Institute of History. He held posts at the State Hermitage Museum, the State Museum of Oriental Art, and headed the Kara-Tepe Archaeological Expedition.

Boris Turayev was a historian who studied at St. Petersburg University and under Adolf Erman. He spent his career teaching at Imperial St. Petersburg University (1896–1918) and Saint Petersburg State University (1918–1920).

Boris Vladimirovich Semichov was a scholar of Tibetology, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Theodore Stcherbatsky from circa 1924 to 1929 and worked at the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts from circa 1929 to 1937.

Boris Vladimirovič Semičëv worked in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, studying at Saint Petersburg State University under Fyodor Shcherbatskoy. He held posts at the Institute of Buddhist Culture, the University of Chicago, and the Buryat Institute of Social Sciences.

Boris Vladimirtsov was a linguist and scholar of Central Asian and Tibetan studies. He studied at Saint Petersburg University and under Antoine Meillet and Paul Pelliot, later holding posts at Saint Petersburg State University and the Institute of Oriental Manuscripts.

Boris Vsevolodovič Miller was a linguist and Central Asian specialist who studied at Moscow State University and the Lazarev Institute. He held posts at Moscow State University, the State Museum of Ethnology, and the Institute of Linguistics.
Bortolo Maria Bortolazzi was an Indology scholar. He served as a Greek teacher at the Ginnasio Comunale di Bassano from 1853 to 1854 and held a post at the Liceo Classico Jacopo Stellini until 1860.
Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima was a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied at Śrī Siṃha Shedra under Tubten Nyendrak, Khenpo Genam, and Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang.

Boyd Michailovsky is a linguist and Tibetologist who earned his Ph.D. from the University of California, Berkeley. He worked as a Directeur de recherche at the Centre national de la recherche scientifique from 1979 to 2010.
Bożena Śliwczyńska is an Indologist who studied under Maria Byrski and is attested as a faculty member at the University of Warsaw in 2026.

Bradford Lyman Phillips is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology who earned degrees from the University of Virginia and Harvard University, studying under David Germano, Cecil Y. Lang, Michael Aris, Masatoshi Nagatomi, and Jeffrey Hopkins.
Bradley L. Herling is a scholar of religious studies and philosophy. He has served as Assistant Director at Boston University and held an attested post at Marymount Manhattan College in 2008.

Braj Basi Lal was an archaeologist and indologist who studied at the University of Allahabad and trained under Mortimer Wheeler. He served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India (1968–1972) and Director of the Indian Institute of Advanced Study (1976–1986).

Brandon Dotson is a Tibetologist and historian who earned his doctorate at the University of Oxford under Charles Ramble and his habilitation at the University of Munich. He held posts at SOAS (2005–2010) and the University of Munich (2010–2019).

Brandon J. Harwood is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies who completed his PhD at the University of Louisville under Patrick Pranke. In 2018, he served as Project Coordinator and Senior Lecturer at the University of Louisville.
